intro: How to read an opinion article: tell the main claim from the evidence and follow an objection.
p.argumento.consejo: It is also the plot of a film: «el argumento». A good argument rests on data.
p.objeción.consejo: You say «poner una objeción». It takes «a»: «una objeción a la propuesta».
p.conclusión.consejo: You say «llegar a una conclusión» and «en conclusión». It ends in «-ión», like «opinión».
p.ventaja.consejo: Its opposite is «inconveniente» or «desventaja». You say «tener ventaja» and «sacar ventaja».
p.inconveniente.consejo: It is the opposite of «ventaja». «No tengo inconveniente en» + infinitive means «I do not mind».
p.desplazamiento.consejo: It comes from «desplazar», to move from a place. «Mis desplazamientos al trabajo son largos».
p.medida.consejo: Two meanings: what is measured («la medida de la mesa») and an action: «tomar medidas».
p.excepción.consejo: You say «la excepción confirma la regla». It is written with «xc»: «ek-thep-THYON».
p.alternativa.consejo: It is feminine: «una alternativa». You say «no hay alternativa» and «buscar una alternativa».
p.productividad.consejo: It ends in «-dad», like «ciudad». You say «aumentar la productividad».
p.propuesta.consejo: It comes from «proponer». You say «hacer una propuesta» and «aceptar una propuesta».
b1.titulo: Follow the argument, not just the topic
b1.texto:
**Three things to look for.** In an opinion article, look for the main idea, the **argumentos** that support it and the **objeciones** the author admits.

**Connectors.** **Sin embargo** introduces a contrast; **por ejemplo** gives an illustration; **por tanto** marks a **conclusión**; **además** adds a reason.

**Claiming is not proving.** An opinion needs a source, an example or a comparison. Words like **algunos**, **en general** or **puede** limit what is said: they stop a **tendencia** from sounding like a rule.

**This text** is a practice article: its **propuestas** are the writer's opinion, not any company's rule.
b2.f0.texto: This article defends flexible hours for the office.
b2.f1.texto: Its main argument is that each person performs better at a different time.
b2.f3.texto: For example, it does not explain how productivity will be measured.
b2.f4.texto: However hard I look for it, I find no data.
b2.f5.texto: The author admits that some people need a fixed schedule.
b2.f6.texto: That exception gives more strength to his proposal.
b2.f7.texto: Therefore, the best measure would be to try it for three months.
b4.titulo: Conceding and qualifying: por más que and como si
b4.texto:
**Por más que** admits a difficulty and carries on. With the **indicative** it talks about something that really happens: **Por más que lo busco, no encuentro ningún dato.** With the **subjunctive**, about something possible: **Por más que parezca urgente, habrá que evaluarlo.**

**Como si + imperfect subjunctive** compares with something unreal: **Sostiene el café como si fuera un pequeño sol.**

**Connectors** to organise the argument: **sin embargo** (contrast), **por ejemplo** (illustration), **por tanto** (conclusion), **además** (addition).
b4.e0.texto: However urgent it may seem, it will have to be evaluated.
b4.e1.texto: She holds the coffee as if it were a little sun.
b4.e2.texto: Therefore, the company should publish the data.
b5.f0.texto: At seven in the morning the train moves slowly through the fog.
b5.f1.texto: The passengers rest their heads against the cold glass and close their eyes.
b5.f2.texto: A woman holds a hot coffee with both hands as if it were a little sun.
b5.f3.texto: The carriage smells of wet coats and lost sleep.
b5.f4.texto: For many of them that journey is the heaviest part of the day.
b5.f5.texto: A flexible schedule does not mean everyone arrives whenever they like.
b5.f6.texto: Those who study in the afternoon cannot always arrive early.
b5.f7.texto: Rules need clear exceptions in order to be fair.
b5.f8.texto: The company should publish data before and after each change.
b5.f9.texto: The goal is an office where a fixed schedule is not the only option.
b6.o0: publicar datos antes y después de cada cambio
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes: she asks for data to check whether the change works.
b6.o1: cerrar la oficina por la tarde
b6.o1.refuerzo: The text does not ask to close the office.
b6.o2.refuerzo: Pay is not mentioned in the text.
b6.pregunta: What does the columnist ask the company to do?
b7.frase: Por más que ____ urgente, habrá que evaluarlo.
b7.o0.refuerzo: That is indicative: it would work if it were a certain fact.
b7.o1.refuerzo: After «por más que» the future is not used.
b7.o2.refuerzo: Yes: «por más que» + subjunctive talks about something possible.
b7.pregunta: Which form does «por más que» take if it is only possible?
b8.frase: Los horarios flexibles necesitan excepciones claras
b9.o0.refuerzo: It marks a conclusion, not a contrast.
b9.o1.refuerzo: Yes: «sin embargo» sets one idea against the previous one.
b9.o2.refuerzo: It gives an illustration, not a contrast.
b11.o0: El tren sale a las siete
b11.o0.refuerzo: It is a fact you can check in the timetable.
b11.o1: Algunos viajeros estudian por la tarde
b11.o1.refuerzo: It is a fact about people; it can be checked.
b11.o2: La empresa debería publicar los datos
b11.o2.refuerzo: Yes: «debería» expresses a recommendation by the writer.
b11.pregunta: Which sentence gives a recommendation, not a fact?
b12.frase: Sostiene el café como si ____ un pequeño sol.
b12.o0.refuerzo: Yes: «como si» + imperfect subjunctive compares with something unreal.
b12.o1.refuerzo: That is indicative; «como si» needs the subjunctive.
b12.o2.refuerzo: That is future; after «como si» comes the subjunctive.
p.artículo.consejo: A text in a newspaper or magazine; the stress is on «TI».
p.defiende.consejo: Third person of «defender», to support an idea with reasons.
p.ejemplo.consejo: The «j» sounds like «h»; «por ejemplo» introduces an example.
p.medirá.consejo: Future of «medir», third person: the «á» marks the future.
p.admite.consejo: Third person of «admitir», to accept or acknowledge something.
p.necesitan.consejo: Third person plural of «necesitar»; the «c» before «e» sounds like «th».
p.fijo.consejo: «Fijo» means fixed; it is the opposite of «flexible».
p.probarlo.consejo: The infinitive «probar» with «lo» attached; the stress stays on «BAR».
p.evaluarlo.consejo: The infinitive «evaluar» with «lo» attached; the stress is on «AR».
p.publicar.consejo: Infinitive of «publicar», to make something public.
p.apoyan.consejo: Third person plural of «apoyar», to support or rest against something.
p.atrasado.consejo: «Atrasado» means late; «llegar atrasado» is to arrive late.
p.estudian.consejo: Third person plural of «estudiar»; the stress is on «TU».
p.normas.consejo: Plural of «norma», a rule people must follow.
p.excepciones.consejo: Plural of «excepción», a case the rule does not cover.
p.horarios.consejo: Plural of «horario», the times set for doing something.
p.flexibles.consejo: Plural of «flexible», which can be adapted.
